messages:
mira: Heads-up — CI regtest flagged a perf regression on PR 6602. Microbench `scheduler_queue` p95 jumped ~25% on the post-merge run. https://ci.redwood.internal/build/6602/artifacts :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
kevin: saw that. failing metric is scheduler_queue.vlatency.p95_on_ingest, delta +170ms vs baseline. reproducible in regtest perf job?
ana: perf-ci bot shows threshold diff, but the test passed functional. it's a microbench threshold fail.
perf-ci: [auto] Threshold diff detected for job `regtest-microbench-scheduler`. Details: baseline=680ms p95, current=850ms p95, threshold=+10%. See artifacts.
sasha: quick glance at flamegraph (linked in artifacts) — there are more ticks in kernel_selector::choose_path and kv_cache::eviction_scan. looks like extra spin in the selector.
mira: PR 6602 touched batching heuristics + small refactor in kernel_selector. suspect the change to "prefer_high_throughput" weight calculation.
kevin: can someone run the perf repro locally? command is: `./tools/regtest/run_microbench --bench scheduler_queue --seed 42 --iters 5000`
ana: ran locally on my workstation (T4 emu), I see similar p95 shift but magnitude is smaller (+12%). attaching abbreviated log: ```2026-03-12T10:12:03 worker[1] select_kernel: chosen=kernel_v2 weight=0.34; latency=2.8ms
2026-03-12T10:12:03 worker[1] kv_cache: eviction_scan cost=1.2ms```
sasha: interesting — in CI the sequences are longer (seq_len distribution skewed), so selector might be choosing different kernels leading to more KV churn. check sequence histogram in the job artifacts.
kevin: bisect idea: revert the weight tweak in kernel_selector (two-line change) and re-run microbench CI. can do a fast candidate revert commit and point the CI to it.
mira: I started a local bisect: `git bisect start --bad HEAD --good refs/tags/perf-stable-2026-03-01` then apply binary search over the merge window. early signs point at commit c1b4d9 (the refactor)
ana: I also profiled with heap-prof and CPU perf. flamegraph snippet shows repeated calls to `choose_path` followed by lock contention on kv_cache::shard_lock. maybe selector now touches cache metadata more often.
kevin: if that's true, a minimal patch to avoid touching cache metadata when only scoring kernels would help — low-risk revert if we can't fix quickly.
sasha: can we run the regtest with `KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1` to get hit/miss logs? might confirm whether eviction rate increased.
perf-ci: queued a rerun of the microbench PR job with env `KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1` and a pinned short-run config to speed it up. job id 7932.
mira: thanks. if CI confirms eviction churn, I'll prepare the revert PR for the weight math and file an issue linking these artifacts.
kevin: also add a quick unit test to assert `selector` doesn't call cache_mutating APIs from scoring path. small lock-proof helps future regressions.
ana: FYI I added a note to the PR: "rollback candidate if regtest perf confirms" and pinged @eng-sre in case we need to throttle rollouts. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [auto] CI rerun 7932 started by perf-ci — ETA ~8m.
mira: update after rerun: CI logs show eviction rate doubled and p95 back to +24%. confirming. I'm opening the revert now.
kevin: cool. please include bisect notes and the perf logs in the revert PR description. thanks everyone for quick triage. :rocket:
